thread:
carol.support: Heads up — ACME Prod opened a ticket: lots of 429s + p99 latency >500ms on their Dedicated pool since ~09:30 UTC. They say traffic is steady but perf dropped. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/acme/prod
ben.runtime: Pulling graphs now. I see a p99 spike and overall throughput drop. Median batch size dropped from ~48 -> ~3 in the last 20m. Tons of tiny batches (<=8 tokens).
alice.ml: Any auth or billing spikes?
carol.support: They had some 401s earlier but ops deployed an auth-fix at 09:10. Billing shows request count increased (customer traffic), but cost jump is from more requests — primary issue is throughput/latency on our side.
ben.runtime: Quick sampler dump from runtime metrics: 
```
small_batch_pct: 68
avg_batch_tokens: 12
median_batch_size: 3
continuous_batch_window_ms: 8
max_batch_tokens: 1024
prefill_token_limit: 64
inflight_prefill_queue: high
packer_strategy: greedy_v2
```
dave.sre: Looks like a microburst pattern of many very short requests from one tenant. That causes the packer to emit many small microbatches and starve larger requests; GPUs are underutilized even though QPS is high. Also autoscaler oscillating (scale up -> ephemeral scale down every ~60s).
elaine.platform: FYI we rolled a packer_strategy tweak yesterday (greedy_v2) and lowered prefill_token_limit to 64 for faster tail latencies. That might interact badly with microbursts.
ben.runtime: My hypothesis: greedy_v2 + short continuous_batch_window_ms + small prefill limit => aggressive flush of tiny batches. Combined with autoscaler reacting to queue length, we get oscillation and poor throughput. Proposed mitigation immediately: increase continuous_batch_window_ms (8 -> 20ms), raise prefill_token_limit (64 -> 256), and bump max_batch_tokens to 4096. Also enable per-tenant fair_shares (fair_share_per_tenant=true) on the affected pool as a guard.
carol.support: Customer asked for quick mitigation — can we canary? They'd prefer we not disrupt other tenants.
ben.runtime: Plan: 1) Canary config on one Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-78). 2) Monitor median batch size, small_batch_pct, p99, and GPU utilization for 10m. 3) If median_batch_size increases and p99 drops -> roll. 4) If regress -> revert. Rollout commands below.
ben.runtime: Repro helper (simulate microburst of short requests):
```
# send many tiny completion requests to target endpoint
for i in $(seq 1 400); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"acme-dedicated-v1","input":"hi","max_tokens":6}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
wait
```
(This should create lots of tiny batches and reproduce the starvation behavior locally against a pool.)
dave.sre: Also collect traces and pprof while running repro: `curl localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/prof.pb` and `kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/runtime -c runtime --since=5m > /tmp/runtime.logs`. Capture queue depth metrics: `runtime.queue_depth{pool="dp-78"}`.
alice.ml: I'll run the repro against staging quantized model to sanity check packer effects.
elaine.platform: I'll open a canary change PR and schedule a controlled apply at 10:30 UTC, tagging oncall. Canary plan included in PR description and rollback steps.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created, severity=P2, assignees=eng-runtime, sres.
carol.support: I told the ACME PM we will canary a config change and update in 30m. Keeping them notified.
dave.sre: Quick follow-up 15m after canary: median_batch_size on dp-78 jumped to ~28, small_batch_pct dropped to 22%, GPU utilization increased ~35%, p99 down ~60%. Autoscale stabilized (no minute-level flapping). Looks promising.
ben.runtime: Good. I'll prepare a staged rollout for the other pools during off-peak windows, and we'll monitor. For long term: consider adaptive continuous window or an admission control that detects many tiny-req bursts and applies per-tenant rate limit/fairness.
carol.support: Thanks — customer is happier. I'll mark ticket updated and loop back with timeline for global rollout.
ben.runtime: Agreed. I'll follow up with runbook entries for packer tuning and a small chaos test to ensure we don't regress. Thanks everyone.
